text:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER (P1) -> infra oncall: multiple serving pods restarting in SEA cluster; RDMA counters showing CRC/seq errors. Incident: https://pd/redwood/inc/2070012345

oncall-sre: acked, paging Sam (primary infra)

Sam: got it, joining. Initial look: serving pool (sea-serve-*) showing a spike in pod restarts ~07:02 UTC. Kube events show OOMKilled + container restarts right after kernel IB messages.

Julia: I'm tailing dmesg on node sea-2-03, seeing repeated entries:
```
mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: EQ async event: type 0x9
mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: IB QP 0x3a failed: -110
mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: CQE CRC error, port 1
```
Matches increased CRC counters in `ibstat` and `perfquery`

Anya: GPU logs also show GDR failures right before process crashes: `gdr_map failed: -22` then `GPU reset detected` in nvidia logs. When GDR breaks, serving runtime hits huge mem pressure trying to reconnect KV cache -> OOM.

Devin: quick health check across requests: 5xx rate for /v1/generate jumped from 0.3% -> 18% for customers in region; p95 latency doubled. Notable customer ABC has retries flooding.

Sam: initial mitigations in progress:
- cordon sea-2-03, sea-2-04 (suspect nodes)
- scale down serving batch size on fallback pool to reduce memory pressure
- enable CPU-fallback model variant for critical customers (route policy)
- create temporary rate limit for non-critical routes

Luis: I'm preparing a kube drain and rolling node out of pool, but worried about triggering more rebalances. Suggest we failover traffic first.

Anya: suggested run to disable GDR (workaround) on affected nodes: add kernel module option: `gdr_enable=0` + restart nvidia. If that prevents CUDA resets we can revert later.

Sam: doing it on sea-2-03 now. Commands: 
```
sudo modprobe -r gdrdrv || true
sudo echo 0 > /sys/module/gdrdrv/parameters/gdr_enable || true
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
# then restart affected serving pods gracefully
kubectl rollout restart deploy/serve-pool-sea -n inference
```

Julia: after disabling GDR on sea-2-03 I still see IB CRC increments but no immediate CUDA reset yet. Pod restarts dropped from 6/min -> 1/min on that node.

infra-bot: Notice: auto-scaler paused for serve-pool-sea to avoid oscillation.

Sam: we're progressively draining sea-2-04 next and applying same gdr_disable. If both nodes stabilize, we can move traffic back slowly.

oncall-sre: handoff note: I'll stay on for next 30m, then hand to Luis if still active.

Devin: customer impact note for support: high error rates and elevated latency for SEA region since 07:02 UTC; some customers are experiencing 5xx and partial responses. Recommend sending status update: "Degraded performance for SEA region, mitigation underway".

Anya: filing hardware ticket with NIC vendor (Mellanox) — CRC errors on RX path. Also scheduling firmware check for HCA and switch ASIC.

Sam: update after action on sea-2-04: disabled GDR, restarted driver, restarted pods. Pod restart rate fell to baseline on both nodes. Request success rate creeping back up.

Julia: digging into switch counters: some ports show mismatch/errors possibly caused by MTU/segmentation with recent config change from blue-green upgrade last week. Recommend verifying MTU on the leaf switches for SEA rack.

Sam: temporary mitigation summary:
- Disabled GDR on two affected hosts (workaround)
- Drained and removed nodes from serving pool to allow warm nodes to absorb traffic
- Routed critical customers to fallback CPU-variant for 10m during rollout
- Paused autoscaler to avoid cascading restarts

Luis: creating follow-up runbook item: if IB CRC spikes + GDR mapping errors -> disable GDR, cordon node, escalate to networking and HW vendor, avoid immediate mass pod restarts.

Anya: opened ticket INC-SEA-2070012345 with vendor. Link: https://tickets/redwood/INC-SEA-2070012345

Devin: support status update sent at 07:25 UTC. Customers notified of degraded performance and that mitigations are in place.

infra-bot: Metrics: 5xx rate in SEA region now down to 2.1% (was 18%). p95 latency back to ~2.1s.

Sam: will keep monitoring for 30m then schedule a maintenance window to roll firmware and re-enable GDR for testing. If CRC errors return we will push a switch/port-level change (MTU/flowcontrol) with networking.

oncall-sre: handing to Luis for next shift. Luis — please ack and continue monitoring + coordinate with networking/vendor.

Luis: acknowledged. I'll keep this open, will update on escalation call. :thumbsup:

-- end thread --
